html:
Mazun was the Persian name for Oman under the Sasanian Empire, from the 3rd century until the coming of Islam. It is shown here in 600 and 700.

The Sasanians held the coast and the fertile inland plains, with the port of Sohar as a key base for Gulf trade. Persian settlers built and kept up the falaj irrigation channels. Arab tribes, above all the Azd, held the mountains and much of the interior, and their leaders, the Julanda family, came to share power with the Persian governor.

Around 630 the Julanda rulers accepted Islam after an envoy from the Prophet Muhammad reached them, and they expelled the Persians. Oman later became a home of the Ibadi branch of Islam. See also Oman in antiquity.
